notes: Identity independently checked: supplied text title Bottomless Bowls: Why Visual Cues of Portion Size May Influence Intake; authors Brian Wansink, James E. Painter, and Jill North; DOI header 10.1038/oby.2005.12; article citation Obes Res. 2005;13:93–100 and journal page footers agree with the neutral original reference. Document contains abstract, methods, results, Tables 1–2, discussion and references: primary journal article text, not an abstract-only excerpt or replication report. No PDF path supplied; no acquisition or rendering performed. Target remains ambiguous: the supplied description of actual and estimated consumption among self-refilling participants could refer to ounce or calorie correlations (Table 2: r = 0.33 with dagger p < 0.05, or r = 0.12 with no numerical p), or a comparison of actual versus estimated intake. The p. 97 narrative gives calorie correlation r = 0.12 for self-refilling participants and actual/estimated calorie means 267.9/127.4; no paired comparison test is printed there. Table 1 reports between-condition F tests separately for actual ounces/calories (8.99, p < 0.01), estimated ounces (0.46) and estimated calories (0.03); these do not identify a unique within-self-refilling actual-versus-estimated target. Candidate sample only: Table 2 explicitly labels self-refilling soup bowls n = 31, normal soup bowls n = 23, all participants n = 54. These are participants, not observations or clusters; exclusions for these final counts are not documented. Do not assign candidate N globally because target test is unresolved. No N is inferred from df, no N sum used, and no effect conversion performed. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
